title: Residual Fisher Information in Measurement-Error Uncertainty
abstract: Measurement error in the Watanabe-Sagawa-Ueda formulation is the excess estimation error of a classical record over the quantum statistical limit. We show that, at the quantum-instrument level, this excess has an exact decomposition. The record-only error matrix equals a residual-aware error matrix plus a positive Schur-complement term fixed by Fisher information left in the unread post-measurement system. Thus measurement error separates into intrinsic instrument loss and record-restriction loss
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to decompose the total measurement error in quantum estimation into two distinct physical components: intrinsic instrument loss and record-restriction loss. By analyzing the structure of the error matrix, it provides a deeper understanding of how measurement limitations arise from both the physical apparatus and the information retained in unread quantum residuals. This has broad implications for quantum sensing and information theory.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the excess estimation error in quantum measurements, specifically decomposing the measurement error uncertainty derived from the Watanabe-Sagawa-Ueda (WSU) formulation.
main_result: The total measurement error separates exactly into two positive semi-definite components: intrinsic instrument loss ($\Delta_{inst}$) and record-restriction loss ($\Delta_{rec}$), providing a fundamental decomposition of measurement uncertainty.
method: The analysis uses quantum information theory tools, relating the error area derived from the full classical-quantum output to bounds involving residual quantum states and Fisher information matrices.
model_or_system: The framework applies to general quantum measurements described by POVMs and quantum instruments, illustrated by an example of single-mode displacement sensing using quadratures (Q and P) via a beam splitter.
key_observables: Measurement Error ($\Delta_{WSU}$), Intrinsic Instrument Loss ($\Delta_{inst}$), Record-Restriction Loss ($\Delta_{rec}$), Quantum Error Area ($B_{AB}$), and various error product bounds ($\epsilon_Y(A)\epsilon_Y(B)$).
important_parameters: The reflectivity $\kappa$ of the beam splitter, which controls the magnitude of the residual information.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a common estimable support for the relevant Fisher matrices, and the decomposition formulas rely on the non-singularity of the record Fisher matrix $J_Y$ for explicit forms.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the structure implies showing the hierarchy of error determinants and the saturation of the residual-improved bounds in the displacement sensing example.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the decomposition theorem for the WSU error matrix, proves the error-area hierarchy relating record-only bounds to the full quantum bound, and then applies this framework to a concrete example (displacement sensing) to demonstrate saturation.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, fundamental decomposition of measurement uncertainty in quantum estimation, which has implications for understanding the limits of sensing in open quantum systems and quantum metrology.
